meta.title: This Week on the News Board
meta.textType: functional: a school news board with four items, one of them a news report

paragraphs: On Monday, February first, Lily and May pinned the weekly news board outside the library door. Teacher Kim checked it before the first bell. The heading said "SCHOOL NEWS," and four notices were under it. Each notice had a small drawing: a racket, a bicycle, a paper lantern, and a young tree. May held a pile of papers. Mia and Leo stopped to read the board. "What is the news this week?" asked Mia.

The first notice was about tennis lessons. It said, "A tennis player from the town club will teach the children." The lessons are on the sports field every Wednesday at four o'clock. "Bring a racket or borrow one," said the notice. Ten rackets are available. So nobody has to buy one. The second notice was about the cycling club. It has a meeting every Friday at half past three. "Bring a helmet," said the notice. "My dad fixes bikes, so my bike is always ready," said Mia. "I can be a member of the cycling club!"

The third notice was a news report with a photo. Its heading said "SEVEN NEW TREES FOR OUR SCHOOL." The article was short, and it told about an event of the week before. "Seven trees were planted near the field on Thursday, January twenty-eighth," the report said. "First the holes were dug, and then the young trees were watered." In the photo, four children stood with spades and a watering can beside a young tree. The line under the photo said, "Our new trees."

The last notice was about the school musical, "The Lantern Show." The auditions are on Monday, February eighth, at lunchtime in the hall. "Come and sing, dance, or play a part," said the notice. The musical will be a big event for the whole school. Leo read the notice twice and smiled. "I cannot sing, but I can paint the lanterns," he said.

Then Leo looked at the news report again. "The report says that seven trees were planted," he said. "Who planted them?" he asked, and he grinned. May laughed and said, "We did, Leo. You held the watering can." "The report does not say who did the work," said Teacher Kim, "but the photo does." "Every notice has a heading," she said, "so a reader finds the main topic at once." "Which notice will you read first?" she asked. "The tennis one," said Lily, "because I want to borrow a racket."
